subject: Discovery recap & PoC onboarding plan — FastRetail
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emma Johnson <emma.johnson@fastretail.com>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com, sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap & PoC onboarding plan — FastRetail

Hi Emma — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned. Please reply with any corrections.

Summary of pain & goals
- Pain: high inference cost and inconsistent latency for real-time product recommendations across peak traffic. Current infra requires manual provisioning and suffers cold-starts.
- Goal: move to a predictable, low-latency inference tier for user-facing recommendations and reduce cost per inference by ~30% while maintaining quality.

Current stack (what you shared)
- Model: in-house transformer (1.3B parameters) served today via Kubernetes with Tesla V100s, bespoke batching.
- Data flow: async feature store -> prediction service -> storefront.
- Languages: primary back-end is Python (FastAPI); front-end calls via REST. You also mentioned some teams prefer Node.js SDK.

Success criteria for PoC
- API integration working with no code-model changes (compatible model artifact).
- P95 latency < 150ms for 512-token requests in the staging region.
- Cost reduction >= 25% versus current baseline (we’ll measure with a 72-hour traffic replay).
- End-to-end quality parity (A/B test against current predictor).

Proposed PoC scope & timeline
1) Week 0 (this week): Align owners, exchange access & security baseline.
2) Week 1: Integration — sandbox API keys, SDK install (Python + Node examples), validate sample requests.
3) Week 2: Traffic replay + load test (collect latency/cost baselines).
4) Week 3: Quality evaluation + A/B sample test.
5) Week 4: Results, decide next steps (Dedicated capacity or rollout).

Owners (from Redwood/your side)
- Redwood AE: Ben Carter (me) — commercial and scheduling
- Redwood SE: Sean Gallagher — integration, load tests, SDK examples
- Redwood CS: Lauren Bishop — success criteria, regression monitoring
- FastRetail: Emma Johnson — technical lead; Liam O'Neill (procurement) — contract/PO

Integration notes / engineering checklist
- SDKs: we’ll provide Python + Node (npm / pip) examples; recommend starting with our Python SDK for FastAPI.
- API compatibility: Standard REST endpoints, JSON payloads; we support streaming + non-streaming responses. No change to your model code required for a standard inference PoC — we can host a compatible variant if needed.
- Auth: API keys to start; KMS/HSM for Private deployments if later required.

Attachments
- FR_PoC_plan_v1.pdf (attached) — detailed milestones and test plan

Next steps / asks
1) Emma/Liam — confirm alignment on the success criteria and PoC timeline above.
2) Emma — share 2 sandbox users or a service account for API key provisioning.
3) Liam — if procurement needs an estimate or SOW to begin approval, I can attach a draft (cc’ing Lauren).
4) Propose a follow-up call on Thu 3/12 @ 10:00am PT to kick off integration — does that work?

Thanks — looking forward to getting started.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

From: Emma Johnson <emma.johnson@fastretail.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@fastretail.com>, lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com, sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 17:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap & PoC onboarding plan — FastRetail

Thanks Ben — this looks accurate and helpful. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Confirmation on pain/goals: yes, exactly. Our primary immediate requirement is to fix P95 latency spikes during flash sales while keeping cost flat or lower.
- Stack note: our model artifacts are exported in ONNX as well as PyTorch; compatibility with either is helpful.
- Security: we will need a completed security questionnaire and SOC 2 evidence before we can start sending any production-like data. Can you share the questionnaire and a copy of your SOC 2 report?
- Procurement: Liam, please flag any procurement timeline constraints. We typically need a signed SOW + PO for vendors before we can spin up reserved capacity — but for the PoC we can run on a hosted test account.

On timeline — Thu 3/12 10:00am PT works for the follow-up call. Please send calendar invite.

A couple of asks for the PoC kickoff:
1) We will provision a service account for sandbox access by EOD Wed (3/11).
2) Can Sean share a short Node example for infer calls? A lot of our frontend services are Node-based and that will help us validate end-to-end quickly.

Thanks,
Emma
Head of ML Platform | FastRetail
emma.johnson@fastretail.com
+1 (212) 555-0124

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>

Great — thanks Emma and Liam. Quick responses:
- SOC 2 & security questionnaire: attaching our standard security packet and a short questionnaire for your security team to fill out. I’ve also added a link to our SOC 2 report in the Google Drive folder (see links below).
- Node example: Sean — can you drop a minimal Node snippet for fast-checking the inference endpoint? Ideally a 5–10 line example that wraps fetch/axios.
- SOW: attaching a draft SOW (FastRetail_SOW_draft.docx) for procurement to review; we can iterate.
- Calendar: follow-up scheduled Thu 12 Mar 2026 10:00am PT — calendar invite sent (see link).

Links & attachments:
- Draft SOW: FastRetail_SOW_draft.docx (attached)
- Security packet + questionnaire: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2bPoCPlan
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/company/FR-2026-031

Next practical steps (for visibility)
- Emma: share sandbox service account creds for E2E tests (we prefer a scoped service account; you can rotate keys after PoC).
- Sean / Lauren: Sean to send Node snippet today; Lauren to prepare baseline regression checks we’ll run during Week 3.

Thanks — I’ll be on the Thu call and will have the SE run through the sample integration.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
